page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 9354P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation operating at a base frequency of 3.25 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, translating to 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong performance across compute and memory subsystems. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng ranks in the top 10%, while multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall within the top 25%. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves top 10% performance in Passmark memory testing, supported by strong uncached read and write memory bandwidths. Cryptographic and vector instruction capabilities are enhanced by hardware support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and AES.

Given the high memory density and dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources, this bare metal instance is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the overhead of virtualization. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference, where it achieves top-tier text generation speeds for 7B parameter models.
